arxiv-1911-01425.title: Improved BiGAN training with marginal likelihood equalization
arxiv-1911-01425.creator: Pablo Sánchez-Martín pablo.sanchez-martin@tuebingen.mpg.de, Pablo M. Olmos olmos@tsc.uc3m.es, Fernando Perez-Cruz fernando.perezcruz@sdsc.ethz.ch
arxiv-1911-01425.description: Abstract We propose a novel training procedure for improving the performance of generative adversarial networks (GANs), especially to bidirectional GANs. First, we enforce that the empirical distribution of the inverse inference network matches the prior distribution, which favors the generator network reproducibility on the seen samples.

arxiv-2006-12106.title: Exploiting Non-Taxonomic Relations for Measuring Semantic Similarity and Relatedness in WordNet Journal: Journal Knowledge base systems
arxiv-2006-12106.creator: Mohannad AlMousa, Rachid Benlamri, Richard Khoury
arxiv-2006-12106.description: Abstract Various applications in the areas of computational linguistics and artificial intelligence employ semantic similarity to solve challenging tasks, such as word sense disambiguation, text classification, information retrieval, machine translation, and document clustering. Previous work on semantic similarity followed a mono-relational approach using mostly the taxonomic relation "ISA".

arxiv-2102-06393.title: Mind the beat: detecting audio onsets from EEG recordings of music listening
arxiv-2102-06393.creator: Ashvala Vinay, Alexander Lerch, Grace Leslie
arxiv-2102-06393.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ashvala Vinay, Alexander Lerch, Grace Leslie. We propose a deep learning approach to predicting audio event onsets in electroencephalogram (EEG) recorded from users as they listen to music. We use a publicly available dataset containing ten contemporary songs and concurrently recorded EEG.

arxiv-2105-02242.title: High Tide: A Systematic Search for Ellipsoidal Variables in ASAS-SN 2021 High Tide: A Systematic Search for Ellipsoidal Variables in ASAS-SN – References
arxiv-2105-02242.creator: D. M. Rowan, K. Z. Stanek, T. Jayasinghe, C. S. Kochanek, Todd A. Thompson, B. J. Shappee, T. W. -S. Holoien, J. L. Prieto
arxiv-2105-02242.description: Abstract The majority of non-merging stellar mass black holes are discovered by observing high energy emission from accretion processes. Here we pursue the large, but still mostly unstudied population of non-interacting black holes and neutron stars by searching for the tidally-induced ellipsoidal variability of their stellar companions.

arxiv-2108-08894.title: Measurement of the Low-temperature Loss Tangent of High-resistivity Silicon with a High Q-factor Superconducting Resonator
arxiv-2108-08894.creator: M. Checchin, D. Frolov, A. Lunin, A. Grassellino, A. Romanenko
arxiv-2108-08894.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Checchin, D. Frolov, A. Lunin, A. Grassellino, A. Romanenko. In this letter, we present the direct loss tangent measurement of a high-resistivity intrinsic (100) silicon wafer in the temperature range from ∼ 70 \sim 70 mK to 1 K, approaching the quantum regime. The measurement was performed using a technique that takes advantage of a high quality factor superconducting niobium resonator and allows to directly measure the loss tangent of insulating materials with high level of accuracy and precision.

arxiv-2110-04611.title: Bogoliubov theory of the laser linewidth and application to polariton condensates
arxiv-2110-04611.creator: Ivan Amelio, Iacopo Carusotto
arxiv-2110-04611.description: Abstract For a generic semi-classical laser dynamics in the complex Ginzburg-Landau form, we develop a Bogoliubov approach for the computation of the laser emission linewidth. Our method provides a unifying perspective of the treatments by Henry and Petermann: both broadening mechanisms are ascribed to the non-orthogonality of the Bogoliubov modes, which live in a space with doubled degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2411-03232.title: A Bayesian Model of Credence in Low Energy Supersymmetry
arxiv-2411-03232.creator: Richard Dawid, James D. Wells
arxiv-2411-03232.description: Abstract We carry out a quantitative Bayesian analysis of the evolution of credences in low energy supersymmetry (SUSY) in light of the most relevant empirical data. The analysis is based on the assumption that observers apply principles of optimism or pessimism about theory building in a coherent way.

arxiv-2510-18614.title: Qatsi: Stateless Secret Generation via Hierarchical Memory-Hard Key Derivation
arxiv-2510-18614.creator: René Coignard Independent Researcher Dessau-Roßlau, Germany Anton Rygin Technische Universität Dresden Berlin, Germany https://github.com/coignard/qatsi
arxiv-2510-18614.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by René Coignard Independent Researcher Dessau-Roßlau, Germany Anton Rygin Technische Universität Dresden Berlin, Germany https://github.com/coignard/qatsi. We present Qatsi, a hierarchical key derivation scheme using Argon2id that generates reproducible cryptographic secrets without persistent storage. The system eliminates vault-based attack surfaces by deriving all secrets deterministically from a single high-entropy master secret and contextual layers. Outputs achieve 103–312 bits of entropy through memory-hard derivation (64–128 MiB, 16–32 iterations) and provably uniform rejection sampling over 7776-word mnemonics or 90-character passwords.

arxiv-2512-24624.title: A Uniform Pilot and Data Payload Optimization Framework for OTFS-Based ISAC
arxiv-2512-24624.creator: Borui Du, Yumeng Zhang, Christos Masouros, Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2512-24624.description: Abstract The orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) signal is considered a promising solution for high-mobility wireless environments. It manages Doppler effects by utilizing delay-Doppler (DD) domain processing. However, the relatively long OTFS frame duration could introduce considerable sensing or communication latency when radar and communication are performed separately.

pmc-11475982.title: Factors Influencing Background Parenchymal Enhancement in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography Images
pmc-11475982.creator: Daniel Wessling, Simon Männlin, Ricarda Schwarz, Florian Hagen, Andreas Brendlin, Sebastian Gassenmaier, Heike Preibsch
pmc-11475982.description: Background: The aim of this study is to evaluate the correlation between background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) and various patient-related and technical factors in recombined contrast-enhanced spectral mammography (CESM) images. Material and Methods: We assessed CESM images from 62 female patients who underwent CESM between May 2017 and October 2019, focusing on factors influencing BPE.

pmc-12425122.description: Optical spectroscopic techniques have been successfully employed in bioprocessing as process analytical technology for real‐time process monitoring in numerous applications. The implementation of spectroscopy‐based PAT techniques commonly necessitates the generation of representative process data used for calibration and validation of multivariate statistical models for analyzing the sample composition in real‐time.

pmc-12467511.title: Pancreatic Solid Pseudopapillary Neoplasms—Clinicopathological Characteristics and Surgical Outcomes: A 10-Year Single-Centre Observational Study
pmc-12467511.creator: Agnieszka Partyka, Wiktoria Bajek, Paulina Wietrzycka, Beata Jabłońska, Sławomir Mrowiec, Maher Y Abdalla
pmc-12467511.description: Background: Pancreatic solid pseudopapillary neoplasms (SPNs) are rare exocrine tumours with predominance in young women. These tumours are of low malignant potential, become considerably large before causing symptoms and are associated with good prognosis. This study aimed to present and analyse clinicopathological features and surgical outcome of SPNs.

pmc-12692126.title: Bioactive Compound Profiling of Agarophyte Seaweed (Gelidiella acerosa, Gracilaria arcuata, and Gracilaria verrucosa) Based on LC-HRMS Metabolomic and Molecular Networking Approach
pmc-12692126.creator: Maria Dyah Nur Meinita, Riyanti, Dyahruri Sanjayasari, Riviani, Dicky Harwanto, Apisada Jiso, Till F. Schäberle, Ute Mettal, Il-Soo Moon, Jae-Suk Choi
pmc-12692126.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To date, exploration of Gracilaria and Gelidiella’s bioactive compounds has been conducted using conventional methods that require a long time, high costs, and significant effort. Currently, metabolomic profiling and molecular networking have emerged as methods of exploring bioactive compounds. This study aimed to perform bioactive compound profiling through a metabolomic LC-HRMS-based and molecular networking approach in Gelidiella acerosa, Gracilaria arcuata, and Gracilaria verrucosa.

pmc-12972723.title: Comparative study on key aroma components of Hongqu Huangjiu with different sugar contents through aroma analysis technology
pmc-12972723.creator: Siman Zheng, Yangyang Huo, Juan Wang, Tianyi Cao, Mingquan Huang, Hongqin Liu, Jihong Wu, Jinglin Zhang, Qing Ren, Dongrui Zhao
pmc-12972723.description: Hongqu Huangjiu (HQHJ) is a representative traditional Chinese fermented beverage with medicinal and nutritional value. However, composition of aroma-active components in HQHJ with different sugar contents remains unclear. Herein, solid-phase extraction combined with gas chromatography–olfactometry–mass spectrometry revealed 56 aroma-active compounds (20 newly identified) in HQHJ. Difurfuryl sulfide was identified as a odorants in Huangjiu for the first time.

pmc-13673593.creator: Chengqiong Mao, Yang Liu, Chao Zhang
